The House impeaches with a simple majority. That's only a charge.

patterns: Hegseth impeachment was the day's biggest story line: 25 hits (~869k views). rawsalerts' 'Massie officially introduces articles of impeachment' got ~269k, and Gunther's defense posts drew the like rates ('Where was the impeachment vote for Lloyd Austin?' ~82k at 14.3%, 'American Hero... ain't going anywhere' ~59k at 13.4%)

Thune blame is still the most reliable engagement lane: 17 hits (~729k) at a 9.5% combined like rate. 'Jim Banks became the SIXTH Republican senator' got ~97k at 15.9% and 'Making Thune Leader was a HUGE mistake' ~61k at 15.0%, ahead of today's leadership vote
Gunther's 'Hey @grok' questions won raw reach but almost no likes: 6 hits (~831k) at about 1.0%. The Bermuda Triangle question topped the board at ~428k (0.6%), and the deportation question got ~175k

Election-count distrust and the Electoral College: 7 hits (~481k). Boebert trailing in a Trump +18 district got ~214k at 4.5%, the Electoral College 'farmer in Iowa' line ~125k at 10.7%, and 'More votes than people' ~54k at 16.9%
Short faith and values one-liners keep the best like rates: 4 scripture/Jesus posts (~260k) at 12.1%, plus 'Islam vs Christianity' ~119k at 13.4%
Tennessee Senate (Tim Burchett for Blackburn's seat): 6 hits (~160k) at 11.5%, led by the Burchett 'Congressional MVP' post at 17.0%
alx's best was the Newsom protein/creatine ban jab (~225k at 4.0%), and rawsalerts' Texas Supreme Court '7 of 9 seats are women' post got ~257k
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, ~20 unique posts) was mostly model-race chatter, and none of it got near the watchlist's reach. Leading posts were @bebuu_ai's leaked Gemini 4 Hydrogen benchmark sheet (~38k), @HarshithLucky3 ranking Claude Fable 5.2 above Gemini 4 Carbon and GPT-6 Astra (~25k), @testingcatalog's daily AI briefs (~18-20k each), and an OpenAI $11B round at a $1.25T valuation (~17k). The Nvidia/Jensen Huang story carried over at low reach, now about Nvidia shares sliding and the board investigating. X News themes were the 'AI slop' label debate, Anthropic's Amodei warning about entry-level job cuts, and developers arguing about AI agents writing code. Gunther's @grok questions (Bermuda Triangle ~428k) were the closest AI-adjacent watchlist hits.
narrative_synthesis: Monday-to-Tuesday window: Massie's impeachment articles against Hegseth and Thune's run for Minority Leader carried the board. Thune blame and Hegseth defense earned 10-16% like rates, while Gunther's '@grok' questions took the most raw views at around 1%. Boebert trailing, the Electoral College and 'more votes than people' kept the election-count lane alive, and Tennessee's Burchett-for-Senate push picked up strong likes. Volume was lighter than recent weekdays (160 originals, 156 hits).
